title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases (For Trial Implementation)
keywords_en: Court handling of juvenile criminal cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Several Provisions on Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases (For Trial Implementation)

Fa (Yan) Fa [1991] No. 7

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC and the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the PRC, and in light of the judicial practice of adjudicating juvenile criminal cases in China, for the purposes of safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of juvenile defendants, lawfully punishing and educating juvenile offenders, ensuring that innocent juveniles are not subject to criminal prosecution, and gradually establishing and improving a juvenile criminal adjudication system with Chinese characteristics.

Article 2 In adjudicating juvenile criminal cases, the facts must be taken as the basis and the law as the criterion. The policy of combining punishment with education shall be adhered to, the principles of education, persuasion, and redemption shall be implemented, and measures for comprehensive management of social order shall be carried out.

Article 3 A people's court shall establish a juvenile court (i.e., a collegial panel for juvenile criminal cases) within its criminal adjudication tribunal. Where conditions permit, a juvenile criminal adjudication tribunal with the same organizational status as other adjudication tribunals may also be established.

The Supreme People's Court and high people's courts shall establish a juvenile court guidance group to guide the work of juvenile courts and to summarize and disseminate experience in juvenile criminal adjudication work.

Article 4 The juvenile court adjudicating first-instance criminal cases shall be composed of judges or of judges and people's assessors, except for minor criminal cases and cases otherwise provided by law. The juvenile court adjudicating second-instance criminal cases shall be composed of judges.

The presiding judge of the juvenile court shall be a judge with broad knowledge, good political and professional competence, familiarity with the characteristics of juveniles, and proficiency in ideological education work for wayward juveniles, and he shall maintain relative stability.

People's assessors of the juvenile court shall generally be persons familiar with the characteristics of juveniles and enthusiastic about educating and redeeming wayward juveniles; specially invited persons such as teachers or cadres from the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, trade unions, schools, or retired personnel may also serve as people's assessors.

The judicial personnel of the juvenile court shall include female judges or female people's assessors.

Article 5 The juvenile court shall, based on the physiological and psychological characteristics of the juvenile defendant, focus on guidance in the mode and method of trial, integrate education with adjudication, combine punishment with education; accurately, promptly, and lawfully ascertain the alleged criminal facts, and assist the juvenile defendant in understanding the causes of the crime and the social harmfulness of the criminal conduct.

Article 6 The scope of cases accepted by the juvenile court:

(1) Where the defendant was under the age of 18 at the time of the commission of the crime;

(2) In joint crime cases, where the principal culprit or principal offender of a criminal group was under the age of 18 at the time of the commission of the crime;

(3) In joint crime cases, where more than one-half of the defendants were under the age of 18 at the time of the commission of the crime.

Whether other criminal cases involving juveniles are to be accepted by the juvenile court shall be decided by the president of the court or the chief judge of the adjudication tribunal. The trial of juvenile defendants shall all be handled with reference to these Provisions.

Article 7 The people's court shall strengthen its connections with public security organs, people's procuratorates, and judicial administrative organs, adhere to the principles of division of responsibilities, mutual coordination, and mutual checks, to ensure accurate and effective implementation of the law and jointly handle juvenile criminal cases well.

Article 8 The people's court shall seek assistance from trade unions, the Women's Federation, the Communist Youth League, juvenile protection organizations, education departments, and other relevant units, to jointly carry out the work of educating and redeeming juvenile defendants.

Article 9 Cases involving juvenile defendants aged 14 or over but under 16 shall not be heard in public.

Cases involving juvenile defendants aged 16 or over but under 18 shall generally not be heard in public. If a public hearing is necessary, it shall be approved by the president of the court or the chief judge of the adjudication tribunal, and the number and scope of observers shall be restricted.

The image of a defendant in a juvenile criminal case that is not heard in public shall not be disclosed in any manner.

If the adult close relatives or teachers of the juvenile defendant attend the court session, which is beneficial to the trial work and to the education and persuasion of the juvenile defendant, they may be permitted or invited to attend with the approval of the chief judge of the adjudication tribunal, but shall not disseminate or provide information on the case proceedings to the outside.

Article 10 The people's court shall lawfully ensure that the juvenile defendant obtains a defense.

The juvenile court shall inform the juvenile defendant and his legal representative that, in addition to defending himself, the defendant may also entrust a defender to defend him.

If no defender has been entrusted, the people's court shall appoint a defender for him.

During the course of the trial, the juvenile defendant may refuse the defender's continued defense or may entrust another defender.

Chapter II Preparatory Work Before Trial

Article 11 After examining a juvenile criminal case initiated by public prosecution, the juvenile court shall decide to open a court session for trial if the facts are clear, the evidence is sufficient, and the case meets the requirements of Article 6 of these Provisions; if the main facts are unclear and the evidence insufficient, the people's court may return the case to the people's procuratorate for supplementary investigation; if no criminal liability need be pursued, the people's procuratorate may be requested to withdraw the prosecution, or the juvenile court may render a judgment based on the facts and the law.

After deciding to open a court session for trial, the presiding judge shall proactively contact the public prosecutor to understand the juvenile defendant's personality, psychological state, and conduct during the investigation and prosecution stages.

Article 12 Before the opening of the court session, the judicial personnel shall carefully review the case file, conduct necessary investigations and home visits, to understand the juvenile defendant's date of birth, living environment, growth process, social contacts, and conduct before and after the alleged crime, and shall examine the alleged criminal facts and motives.

Article 13 The juvenile court may, with the assistance of family and social forces, conduct legal education and propaganda for the juvenile defendant through forums and other forms, and provide necessary assistance.

Article 14 When serving a copy of the bill of indictment on a juvenile defendant, the juvenile court shall explain to the defendant the alleged crime and relevant legal provisions, explain relevant policies; and point out that when facing trial, he should truthfully answer the court's questions.

Article 15 Before the opening of the court session, the juvenile defendant's understanding and opinions on the alleged crime shall be ascertained.

Article 16 The juvenile court shall provide guidance and education to address the juvenile defendant's ideological concerns, fear, and antagonistic emotions.

Article 17 For new facts and evidence raised by the juvenile defendant, his legal representative, or defense counsel, the people's court may return the case to the people's procuratorate for supplementary investigation; the juvenile court may also conduct its own investigation, collect and obtain evidence, and conduct new inquests and appraisals.

Article 18 When serving a copy of the bill of indictment on the juvenile defendant's legal representative, the juvenile court shall inform him of his rights, obligations, and matters to note during the court session.

Article 19 Before the opening of the court session, if the juvenile court deems it necessary, it may arrange for the juvenile defendant's legal representative or other guardian to meet with the juvenile defendant. Judicial personnel shall be present.

Article 20 If the juvenile defendant's legal representative or other guardian has had a negative influence on the juvenile defendant's growth or has provided improper education, the judicial personnel shall urge self-education on their part.

The juvenile court shall inform the juvenile defendant's legal representative or other guardian that they shall not shirk responsibility nor interfere with the trial.

Article 21 The juvenile court shall provide defense counsel with convenient access to case files and time to meet with the juvenile defendant. Judicial personnel may also inform defense counsel of relevant provisions on adjudicating juvenile criminal cases.

Article 22 The work and activities conducted by the juvenile court before trial shall be recorded and filed.

Chapter III Trial

Article 23 The juvenile court shall set a seat for the juvenile defendant's legal representative on the side of the defense table near the observer area.

Article 24 The juvenile defendant may sit when answering questions in court.

Restraints shall not be used on the juvenile defendant in court. Judicial police may not stand in the courtroom but shall enter to maintain order.

Article 25 The juvenile court shall inform the juvenile defendant in detail of the procedural rights lawfully enjoyed, such as the right to apply for recusal, to defend, to ask questions, to present new evidence, to apply for a new appraisal or inquest, and to make a final statement, and shall ensure the exercise of the above rights.

Article 26 Before the opening of the court session, the juvenile court shall notify the juvenile defendant's legal representative to appear in court. If the legal representative's presence hinders or interferes with the juvenile defendant's normal answers and statements, the presiding judge may stop him or order him to leave the court. If the legal representative is not suitable to appear in court, the juvenile court may replace him with another guardian or close relative to appear.

The legal representative shall enjoy procedural rights in court, including the right to apply for recusal, to ask questions, and to defend. After the juvenile defendant's final statement, with the permission of the presiding judge, the legal representative may also speak.

Article 27 During the court trial, judicial personnel shall, based on the juvenile defendant's intellectual development level and psychological state, pay attention to easing the courtroom atmosphere, achieve case-specific adjudication and individualized education. The attitude of the judicial personnel shall be calm yet dignified, the language both accurate and easy to understand, with an emphasis on guidance while preventing induced interrogation.

Article 28 During court investigation, the juvenile defendant's age at the time of the incident shall be carefully verified. While ascertaining the case facts and verifying the evidence, the subjective and objective causes of the offense shall also be ascertained.

Article 29 During the court proceedings, reprimanding, ridiculing, or threatening the juvenile defendant shall not be allowed. If such occurs, the court shall immediately stop it.

Article 30 After the court investigation and debate, based on the circumstances of the trial, in-court education may be conducted. The public prosecutor and participants in the proceedings may make statements concerning the following:

(1) Educating the juvenile defendant to correctly face the trial;

(2) The harm of the criminal conduct to society and the penal punishment to be imposed;

(3) Analyzing the subjective and objective causes of the socially harmful conduct and the lessons to be learned.

Article 31 Upon adjournment, the legal representative or other guardian may be permitted to meet with the juvenile defendant and to educate him. Judicial personnel or judicial police shall be present.

Article 32 The pronouncement of judgment on a defendant under the age of 18 shall be conducted in public, but a mass meeting shall not be convened.

If a judgment is pronounced at a mass meeting in a joint crime case involving a defendant under the age of 18, that defendant shall not appear.

Article 33 When pronouncing judgment, the juvenile court shall explain to the juvenile defendant the criminal facts found in the judgment, the penalty imposed, and the legal basis and reasons for heavier or aggravated punishment, lighter or mitigated punishment, or exemption from criminal punishment, or acquittal.

For a defendant sentenced to public surveillance or to criminal detention with a suspended sentence, fixed-term imprisonment with a suspended sentence, or death penalty with a two-year reprieve, the relevant legal provisions shall be explained in detail.

Article 34 When pronouncing a guilty verdict, the juvenile defendant shall be educated on admitting guilt, accepting the law, accepting rehabilitation, and repenting and starting anew.

Article 35 When pronouncing judgment, the juvenile defendant's legal representative shall be notified to appear in court, and a copy of the judgment shall be served on the legal representative.

For a case with an incidental civil action in criminal proceedings, the juvenile court shall explain the civil compensation liability to be borne by the juvenile defendant's legal representative.

Article 36 The juvenile defendant shall be clearly informed of the right to appeal, and the legal provision that an appeal shall not result in a heavier punishment shall be explained.

During the appeal period, both the juvenile defendant under the age of 18 and his legal representative shall lawfully have the right to appeal; if the defendant has reached the age of 18, any request by his former legal representative, defender, or other close relatives to appeal must obtain the defendant's consent.

Article 37 Appeals and protests decided to be heard in court shall be handled with reference to the above provisions.

Article 38 If the people's court of second instance upholds or alters the original judgment or ruling, it shall explain to the appellant the reasons and grounds for upholding or altering the judgment.

If the people's court of second instance pronounces the juvenile defendant guilty, it shall continue to conduct education work with the juvenile defendant to consolidate and expand the effect of the case handling.

Article 39 If the judgment acquits the juvenile defendant or exempts him from criminal punishment, or imposes criminal detention with a suspended sentence or fixed-term imprisonment with a suspended sentence, the defendant, if in custody, shall be released immediately after the pronouncement.

Article 40 Juvenile criminal cases in which the intermediate people's court imposes the death penalty with a two-year reprieve shall be subject to approval by the high people's court. In addition to verifying the facts and evidence according to law, the juvenile defendant's age must be verified.

Article 41 The juvenile court shall inform the juvenile defendant and his legal representative of the right to petition against the final judgment or ruling.

Chapter IV Enforcement

Article 42 For juvenile offenders who are taken into custody to serve their sentences, the juvenile court shall conscientiously and carefully fill out a case closure registration form, and shall serve it together with a copy of the effective judgment and the execution notice on the executing authority.

Article 43 For juvenile offenders sentenced to public surveillance, or to criminal detention with a suspended sentence, or to fixed-term imprisonment with a suspended sentence, the people's court may assist the public security organs in jointly formulating assistance and education measures with the offender's original school, work unit, neighborhood committee, villagers' committee, or guardian, and shall conduct necessary follow-up visits.

Article 44 The people's court may establish contact with juvenile correctional facilities through various means, understand the rehabilitation situation of juvenile offenders, and assist juvenile correctional facilities in carrying out assistance, education, and rehabilitation work.

The people's court may conduct follow-up visits to juvenile offenders currently serving sentences at regular or irregular intervals.

Article 45 For written opinions submitted by the executing authority according to law on granting commutation of sentence or parole to a juvenile offender, the people's court shall promptly review and render a ruling. In granting commutation of sentence or parole to juvenile offenders, the people's court may appropriately relax the standards compared to adult offenders according to law.

Article 46 For petitions filed by juvenile offenders in custody and their family members, the people's court shall designate personnel to handle them promptly.

If a juvenile criminal petition case has been delayed without conclusion, the high people's court may instruct the lower people's court to complete it within a time limit and report the results.

Article 47 If a juvenile offender sentenced to public surveillance, or to criminal detention with a suspended sentence, or to fixed-term imprisonment with a suspended sentence, meets the conditions for schooling or employment, the people's court shall submit a judicial recommendation concerning his placement to the relevant department, along with necessary materials.

Article 48 The juvenile court shall urge the parents or other guardians of juvenile offenders taken into custody to serve sentences to visit them promptly, so that the juvenile offenders regain care from family and society and enhance their confidence in rehabilitation.

For juvenile offenders sentenced to public surveillance, or to criminal detention with a suspended sentence, or to fixed-term imprisonment with a suspended sentence, the juvenile court shall timely visit the parents or other guardians of the juvenile offenders to understand their management and education of the juvenile offenders, guide them to correctly assume the responsibility of discipline and education, ensuring neither overindulgence nor discrimination, and creating a favorable environment for the juvenile offenders to turn over a new leaf.

Chapter V Supplementary Provisions

Article 49 Litigation case file materials of juvenile criminal cases shall not be inspected or excerpted without authorization, nor shall they be disclosed or disseminated.

Article 50 These Provisions are adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and shall be implemented on a trial basis from February 1, 1991.

January 26, 1991
